subject: Private connectivity: route filter + SG blocking causing fragmentation errors
messages:
From: Daniel Morris <daniel.morris@stonebridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent drops to Redwood private deployment after capacity bump

Marissa,

We're seeing intermittent TCP sessions drop from our on-prem app servers to the private deployment in your VPC. Symptoms: long-tail tail latency for some connections, retransmits, and occasional 'Fragmentation needed but DF set' ICMPs. Issue started ~36 hours after we increased throughput on our Direct Connect.

Attached is a short tcpdump and a couple traceroutes (tcpdump-stonebridge.pcap). The interesting part is that when packets go via the Direct Connect path they arrive but we never see the return flow hit the same SNAT mapping. When we enabled MSS clamping on our edge (to 1400) the problem decreased for short-lived flows.

Can you triage? We're blocked from going GA if this persists. Happy to join a call.

- Daniel
Network Engineering
Stonebridge Health
Phone: +1 415-555-0142

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Morris <daniel.morris@stonebridge.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent drops to Redwood private deployment after capacity bump

Daniel — thanks for the bug report and the pcap. Looping in our private-deploy networking leads.

Quick plan:
- Can you confirm the exact VPC CIDRs you see in the trace and the DX / VPN path you're using?
- Please send AWS VPC route table for the affected AZ, the Security Group IDs on the ALB and the worker subnet, and a short sample of VPC flow logs for one of failed connection attempts.

Initial remediation we will evaluate: MSS clamp on the peering, validate route filters (advertised prefixes from your edge shouldn't be leaking into our regional route table), and confirm NAT gateway/ALB statefulness isn't dropping SNAT mappings under ECMP or asymmetric routing.

Propose a 30-minute call today at 13:00 PT to run the checklist and, if needed, do a coordinated rollback. Attached: initial-triage-checklist.pdf.

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Daniel Morris <daniel.morris@stonebridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent drops to Redwood private deployment after capacity bump

On Sat, Jun 12, 2027 at 09:35 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Daniel — thanks for the bug report and the pcap. Looping in our private-deploy networking leads.

Quick look at the trace: I see signs of route leakage. Our BGP table for the regional edge shows an extra /19 learned from Stonebridge DX that shouldn't be injected into the per-customer VPC route target. When ECMP hashes pick that path for return traffic it looks like the SNAT mapping on our NAT gateway doesn't get the expected return, so the on-prem sees no matching flow.

Snippets I pulled (sanitized):
- vpc-route: 10.40.0.0/16 -> local
- learned: 10.100.0.0/19 -> dx-peer-3 (unexpected)

Action items I need from Stonebridge: VPC flow logs around the failed timestamps, and a short fw rule dump. From our side I'll diff the route table snapshots (attached route-diff.txt) and validate if we have per-customer route filters misapplied after the recent capacity change.

Temporary mitigation I propose: 1) Add an SG rule to allow ephemeral return ports from your DX peer (owner-managed exception) and 2) temporarily prefer the private VPC path over the leaked path via route target change until we fix the filter. Both are low-risk if coordinated.

- Jonas
Network Lead, Private Deployments

From: Daniel Morris <daniel.morris@stonebridge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudNet Support <support@cloudnetops.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent drops to Redwood private deployment after capacity bump

Jonas — thanks. Quick firewall excerpt attached (fw-config.txt). We are performing SNAT on our ASA and we do see mapping churn under high connection churn. Two notes:
- When we enable MSS clamp at the ASA to 1400 bytes the number of dropped flows drops dramatically.
- Our perimeter is currently dropping ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) because of a policy change last quarter. That prevents PMTUD from converging on the correct path MTU.

We can open the ICMP code 4 temporarily and put MSS clamp in place if that helps. We can be on the 13:00 PT call.

- Daniel

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Morris <daniel.morris@stonebridge.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent drops to Redwood private deployment after capacity bump

Thanks all. Based on the data:
- Confirmed mismatch: leaked prefix from DX caused asymmetric return.
- PMTUD failure: Stonebridge perimeter drops ICMP frag-needed.

Recommended immediate steps (canary, short maintenance window):
1) Stonebridge: enable ICMP type 3 code 4 for a 2-hour window and apply MSS clamp=1400 at perimeter. (Owner: Stonebridge Network)
2) Redwood: add temporary SG egress rule allowing return ephemeral ports from Stonebridge DX peer and set route preference to favor the VPC local path for the affected prefixes. (Owner: Jonas)
3) After 2 hours, collect VPC flow logs and confirm no packet drops; if success, revert SG exception and push permanent route-filter fix into the next config deploy.

I've documented the rollback steps and verification in rollback-playbook.md (attached). Jonas — please coordinate the config push and add tests to ensure SNAT mappings persist under ECMP. Marissa — please confirm we have approval for the temporary security exception.

- Laura
Senior Infra Eng, Redwood

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Daniel Morris <daniel.morris@stonebridge.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent drops to Redwood private deployment after capacity bump

Summary / action items:
- Stonebridge: enable ICMP type 3 code 4 for 13:30-15:30 PT tomorrow and apply MSS clamp=1400 on ASA. (Owner: Daniel)
- Redwood: Jonas will add temporary SG egress rule and change route preference to favor local VPC path for affected prefixes at 13:25 PT. (Owner: Jonas)
- Verification: collect VPC flow logs and tcpdump during the window; Laura will run the post-check playbook and confirm. (Owner: Laura)
- Rollback: if packet drops persist, revert route preference and remove SG exception; document and escalate to infra config team.

Marissa — please confirm this communication reaches the Stonebridge change–approval contact and that the 13:30 window is acceptable. I'll join the runbook call and record the steps.

Thanks everyone — resolving this is high priority for the Stonebridge GA timeline.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
